newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bond yields build in best case scenario.
newsitem.headline: Australia bond yields build in best case scenario.

text.p: FUTURES CASH YIELD
*Australian bond yields dropped sharply again on Wednesday as the market continued to price in all the possible positive data news in the coming weeks, risking a sell-off on the fact.
*U.S. faces housing, industrial production data later today.
Australian bond yields dropped sharply again on Wednesday with already bullish sentiment gaining a further fillip from a rebound in U.S. Treasuries.
The market continued to price in all the possible market friendly news due in the coming weeks on inflation and wages, which some analysts feel is risking a sell-off when the data becomes fact.

The first key figure is next week's March quarter CPI which is widely expected to be benign, although Annette Beacher, senior economist at Citibank Australia, feels the market is heading for a re-run of the reaction to the fourth quarter CPI.

"The December quarter figures, they were great numbers, but the market had convinced itself so much that they were going to be brilliant that the market rallied into them and dropped when they were released," Beacher said.

However, traders feel the market is being well supported at current levels and could rally again on Wednesday should the U.S. hold up after a series of data later on Wednesday, having absorbed profit-taking from domestic institutions.
"The market feels that it wants to go again and could test the low 91.200s (on the 10-year bond futures contract) tomorrow," one trader said.

The June contract struck its highest level since last February at 92.180, although almost half the day's volume was conducted in the first 30 minutes of trading with U.S. hedge funds noted as short covering.

Although domestics were seen offering both government and semi stock, traders said offshore investors remain comfortable with current levels, and European investors were notable buyers in after hours trading prior to the U.S. CPI.
Meanwhile, the Westpac consumer sentiment survey for April showed a modest 0.7 percent fall, its first stable outcome after a particularly volatile six month period.
